Verizon's CEO said today that SpaceX will need at least 4-6 years and $300B-$500B to fully build out its @Starlink Mobile U.S. carrier network:

"Their service just can't compete with a terrestrial network. In suburban and urban areas, where 98% of our revenues are, we're somewhere between 100x–1,000x more efficient than they are. We know exactly what they're going to do. We know who they're talking to on towers. There's no magic wand. There's no secret sauce. There's no shortcut.

They're going to look at 65,000–80,000 macro sites. They're going to need backhaul, RAN, and a tremendous amount of spectrum. It's going to take a minimum of four to six years to fully build that out. It's going to cost hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars, I assume somewhere between $300 billion and $500 billion.

Then they need to build retail, customer service, back office systems, et cetera. All of that gets them basically the same network and same capabilities and same cost structure as what we have today. Then sometime over the next four to six years, they have the possibility of becoming the sixth, not the fourth, the sixth competitor in the market.

You can be sure over these next three to five years or six years, we are not going to be standing still. Four to five years from now, we will be two to three generations better than where we are today. We will have high-speed broadband gig-plus coverage across the country with our millimeter wave. We are ahead of most people and already experimenting with what 6G applications will look like."

(via Verizon's Q3 earnings call earlier this morning)
tweets.text_zh:
Verizon 首席执行官今天表示，SpaceX 将需要至少 4-6 年时间和 300B-500B 美元才能全面建设其 @Starlink Mobile 美国运营商网络：

“他们的服务无法与地面网络竞争。在我们 98% 的收入所在的郊区和城市地区，我们的效率比他们高 100 倍到 1,000 倍。我们确切地知道他们要做什么。我们知道他们在塔上与谁交谈。没有魔杖。没有秘密武器。没有捷径。

他们将查看 65,000–80,000 个宏站点。他们将需要回程、RAN 和大量频谱。完全建立起来至少需要四到六年的时间。这将花费数百亿美元，我假设在 3000 亿到 5000 亿美元之间。

然后他们需要构建零售、客户服务、后台系统等。所有这些使他们拥有与我们今天基本相同的网络、相同的功能和相同的成本结构。然后在未来四到六年的某个时候，他们有可能成为市场上的第六个，而不是第四个，第六个竞争对手。

你可以肯定，在接下来的三到五年或六年里，我们不会停滞不前。四到五年后，我们将比今天进步两到三代人。我们将通过毫米波在全国范围内实现高速宽带千兆以上覆盖。我们领先于大多数人，并且已经开始试验 6G 应用的样子。”

SpaceX has officially announced that they have secured $40 billion in the largest GPU financing ever.

The company entered into a $40B master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing ever.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen:
"SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we're seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers."

Transaction Details:
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

SpaceX 首席财务官布雷特·约翰森：
“SpaceX 的目标是部署世界上最大的计算基础设施。随着对计算的需求持续加速，我们的 SI 基础设施投资回收期不到一年。这次租赁使我们的资金来源多样化，并解决了实现我们的增长计划所需的大部分资金，因为我们的目标是以创纪录的速度在线获取更多计算，为企业和消费者提供动力，为 Grok 提供动力，并为现有和未来的云服务客户提供服务。”

交易详情：
此次融资由阿波罗和高盛牵头的多家融资方承诺，高盛担任独家结构代理。签订租赁合同仍需满足某些特定的成交条件，预计将于 2026 年底前完成，租赁时间表预计将于 2027 年上半年交付 GPU 及相关设备后开始。

THE BORING COMPANY HQ: Bastrop, Texas, October

Here is my flyover of TBC's Bastrop headquarters and Prufrock factory. It's is where they test every machine before it ships, build and store equipment, precast tunnel segments, liner trucks, vertical cassettes and conveyor belt systems, and more. They house their Prufrock Command Center here to control all the Prufrock's soon to be around the world.

- The SpaceX Pedestrian Tunnel started as Porpoise Test 6 (PT6). TBC first bored it to test (no people in the tunnel) ZPIT continuous mining, an upgraded liner truck and the "SNAILS on RAILS" navigation system. After the test, they turned it into a 500 ft walkway under FM1209 that connects the SpaceX site to Hyperloop Plaza, where The Boring Bodega is. People use it so they don't have to cross that busy road on foot.
 
- Hard-rock Prufrock-MB4 being constructed for Nashville's Music City LOOP.

- The Test Tunnel PT5 connects SpaceX's Starlink factory to TBC under FM1209. It was the first use of custom hexagonal segments, automated gantry steering, quick craneless retrieval, and the first version of ZPIT. It's now a test bench for liner trucks, vertical cassettes and new belt systems.

- Hyperloop Test Tunnel was PT4; the first craneless, pitless retrieval of the machine. It's now a vacuum tunnel for Hyperloop vacuum pump system testing. It also connects SpaceX's Starlink factory to TBC under FM1209.

- Lastly, Prufrock-5 after completing a test tunnel connecting Ring Ranch and possibly the SpaceX Starmind Factory. I videoed it right before it was loaded up and shipped to San Antonio, Texas, for the Morgan's Wonderland Tunnel.

If you have any questions, leave them in the comments. Subscriber Photo-thread and Support links in the thread.

Thanks for watching!

Legacy cell carriers a few months ago: Starlink Mobile will not be a competitor. Their signal won’t even be able to penetrate walls.

Legacy cell carriers today: Oh shit, we were wrong. Quick, start lobbying so they can’t compete!

SpaceX plans to launch their next-gen Starlink Mobile service, built for 5G speeds, in early 2028.


Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt)

AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile are jointly lobbying the FCC to preserve existing rules as @SpaceX moves closer to launching its own independent cellular network that would compete directly with the three major U.S. carriers.

On Oct 20th, reps from all three major U.S. wireless carriers met with FCC officials to push back against proposed changes that would give satellite companies more freedom to offer cellular service.

The carriers urged the FCC to:
• Block satellite companies from using certain 5G frequencies currently used by wireless carriers.
• Keep rules requiring satellite companies to get permission from wireless carriers before using their licensed spectrum.
• Allow wireless carriers to maintain control over these agreements, including the ability to end them.
• Reconsider proposed interference limits to protect existing cellular networks.

Based on all the public communications from these carriers, and the lobbying, they are clearly worried that SpaceX's @Starlink Mobile network is going to be a major competitor to them. Starlink Mobile will become the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum.

The FCC recently announced that they are considering new rules that could make it easier for satellite companies like SpaceX to offer cellular service without relying as heavily on existing wireless carriers, so this is partly what the three big carriers are fighting against.

索耶·梅里特（@SawyerMerritt）

AT&T、Verizon 和 T-Mobile 正在联合游说 FCC 保留现有规则，因为 @SpaceX 更接近推出自己的独立蜂窝网络，该网络将与美国三大运营商直接竞争。

10 月 20 日，美国三大无线运营商的代表会见了 FCC 官员，反对允许卫星公司更自由地提供蜂窝服务的拟议变更。

运营商敦促 FCC：
• 阻止卫星公司使用无线运营商目前使用的某些5G 频率。
• 保留要求卫星公司在使用其许可频谱之前获得无线运营商许可的规定。
• 允许无线运营商保持对这些协议的控制，包括终止这些协议的能力。
• 重新考虑提议的干扰限制以保护现有的蜂窝网络。

NHTSA announced today that they are proposing new rules aimed at removing U.S. federal regulatory barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as @Tesla's Cybercab.

The proposed changes include:
• Eliminating requirements for manually operated turn signal controls in vehicles without steering wheels or pedals: "NHTSA has concluded that the self-canceling and manually operated control requirements in the current standard are unnecessary for turn signal operating units that are installed on vehicles without manually operated driving controls."

• Allowing autonomous driving systems to control turn signals, hazard lights, and high/low beams without traditional driver-operated switches.

• Removing certain dashboard indicator requirements for turn signals and high beams in vehicles without manual driving controls.

• Allowing optional cyan-colored exterior lights to indicate when a vehicle is operating autonomously, with standardized requirements for their placement, brightness, and operation.

• Eliminating outdated restrictions on vertical headlight arrangements, giving automakers greater design flexibility.

• Allowing modern integrated headlights to be tested at manufacturer-specified voltages rather than requiring 12.8 volts.

NHTSA says the changes are intended to eliminate unnecessary regulatory barriers, reduce costs, and enable innovation without compromising vehicle safety.

拟议的变更包括：
• 消除不带方向盘或踏板的车辆中对手动操作转向信号控制装置的要求：“NHTSA 得出的结论是，对于安装在不带手动操作驾驶控制装置的车辆上的转向信号操作装置，当前标准中的自取消和手动操作控制要求是不必要的。”

• Tesla is developing its own AI-based mapping and navigation system that will rely on intelligence gathered from its vehicle fleet rather than traditional third-party mapping systems. The system will support conversational voice commands, personalized routing preferences, improved parking, and more intelligent destination handling.

•  Tesla plans to launch Cybercab service in Dallas in November 2026, followed by additional cities.

• Tesla plans to progressively extend robotaxi operating hours, with the goal of reaching 24/7 service by the end of 2026. Tesla expects to expand service to highways, higher-speed roads, additional weather conditions, and nighttime operations by the end of 2026.

• Elon expects Robotaxi to begin making a noticeable contribution to Tesla's financial results around Q2 2027, potentially becoming a significant business by Q3 or Q4 2027.

• Tesla is targeting the first deliveries of Cybercabs to fleet owner customers by the end of 2026, but Elon said the vast majority of Cybercabs will be Tesla-owned and operated as transportation-as-a-service vehicles rather than sold directly to consumers.

• Tesla has started early Optimus production. Elon said: "The growth of Optimus is an S curve, but the initial curve is a shallow slope. There's still some things we need to tweak about the design. There's still quite a lot of work to do with the AI in the robot. I would expect that the AI, the electromechanical design, reliability, usage life, expect these issues to be solved by the end of next year."

• Elon said most of the equipment for an Optimus production line designed to manufacture approximately 1 million robots annually is already at Fremont. Elon expects it will take at least another year, possibly longer, to reach an annualized production rate of approximately 1 million Optimus robots, equivalent to roughly 20,000 per week.

• Elon said Tesla may release a new Optimus V3 demonstration video within one or two months, saying  that it should show genuinely AI-driven tasks rather than preprogrammed movements.

• Tesla is targeting mid-2027 to integrate its AI5 chip into Optimus.

• Management said Optimus production costs are trending toward the expected manufacturing cost of Cybercab, although the robot's design is still being refined.

• Tesla hopes to manufacture its first experimental semiconductor chips around May or June 2027. Tesla is targeting useful chip production at volume in Terafab around Q3 2028.

Here are all the most important highlights from @SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings report and earnings call:

• Total revenue: $14.58B, up 161% YoY from $5.58B and up 87% QoQ from $7.81B.

• Adjusted EBITDA: $8.81B, up 306% YoY from $2.17B and up 149% QoQ from $3.54B.

• Total Capex: $19.59B, up 185% YoY from $6.88B and 7% QoQ from $18.37B, primarily driven by SI infrastructure investments.

• Q4 Capex guidance: SpaceX expects capital expenditures of $35B–$40B in Q4 2026 as it accelerates SI compute deployment.

• Net income: $4.40B, compared to a $1.05B loss a year earlier.

• Income from operations: $2.79B, compared to a $273M loss YoY and a $143M loss in Q2.

• Q1 2027 revenue guidance: $33B–$37B in total revenue during Q1 2027.

• Annualized revenue target: SpaceX remains on track for $100B in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, based on December's revenue run rate.

• Elon's 2027 revenue projection: SpaceX could reach $500B–$1T in annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027

• Backlog: Reached $63B as of September 30, including $17.5B in deferred revenue. ~$42B is expected to be recognized within the next 12 months.

• Space revenue: $1.77B, up 6% YoY

• Connectivity revenue: $5.25B, up 69% YoY and 22% QoQ; Consumer revenue was $3.12B (+57% YoY) and Enterprise & Government revenue was $2.13B (+91% YoY).

• Connectivity operating income: $2.37B, up 99% YoY from $1.19B and 43% QoQ from $1.66B.

• Starlink subscribers: 13.6M, up 89% YoY; consumer ARPU increased to $69/month from $66 in Q2.

• Super Intelligence (SI) revenue: $7.56B, up 830% YoY and 195% QoQ

• SI operating income: Positive $431M, compared to a $1.72B loss YoY and a $1.26B loss in Q2.

• SI Adjusted EBITDA: Positive $4.95B, compared to a $428M loss a year earlier and $1.15B in Q2.

• SI Capex: $16.44B, up 245% YoY from $4.76B and 4% QoQ from $15.83B, representing ~84% of total quarterly Capex spend.

• Cloud Services Agreements: Signed additional agreements during Q3, with SI solutions and infrastructure revenue growing 192% QoQ excluding Cursor.

• SI compute economics: Newly deployed compute capacity is generating payback periods of less than 12 months at current pricing, which is slightly above the previously discussed $30–$50 per watt range.

• Cursor revenue: Contributed $608M in revenue between August 14 and September 30.

• Grok Bot: Reached 800,000 paid weekly users in early October, more than doubling over the prior month.

• Grok Bot enterprise rollout expected in a few weeks.

• Cash, cash equivalents & marketable securities: Approximately $90B at quarter-end

• Operating cash flow: Generated $13.1B during the first nine months of 2026, up 218% from $4.12B during the same period in 2025.

• Starship Flight 15: Targeted for November 2026, with SpaceX planning to attempt a tower catch of Starship's upper stage.

• National Security launches: Secured 18 additional National Security Space Launch missions.

• Starlink aviation: More than 3,800 aircraft were equipped with Starlink as of September 30.

• Starlink aviation contracts: ~12,000 aircraft are now under contract for Starlink service, representing nearly a quarter of the available commercial aircraft market.

• Starlink Mobile users: Surpassed 22M monthly users at the end of Q3, up 37% QoQ.

• Starlink Mobile U.S. launch: SpaceX plans to integrate its spectrum acquisitions and begin activating the expanded service in early 2028, with the gaol of becoming a major U.S. mobile carrier.

• SI compute: Expanded nameplate compute capacity to 1.7 GW, up from 1.4 GW in Q2 and 0.6 GW a year earlier.

• October compute target: SpaceX expects to reach nearly 2 GW of nameplate compute capacity by the end of October 2026.

• Year-end compute target: SpaceX expects 2.5–3 GW of nameplate compute capacity by the end of 2026.

• 2027 compute target: Elon expects to add at least 10 GW of incremental compute capacity in 2027, potentially bringing the total to 13 GW or more. Elon said there is a small possibility of exceeding 20+ GW of active SI compute by the end of 2027.

• GPU deployments: SpaceX is bringing approximately 200,000–220,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs online monthly, with plans to maintain or accelerate that pace.

• Nvidia Vera Rubin deployment: SpaceX expects its 2027 compute expansion to rely primarily on NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin architecture.

• SpaceX plans to bring a training cluster with 440,000 Vera Rubin computers online by the end of Q2 2027.

• Targeting May or June 2027 for the first functional test chips from the Austin research fab.

• Terafab mass production: SpaceX is targeting Q3–Q4 2028 for potential volume chip production at its Gibbons Creek facility

Tesla has officially announced that it will hold its annual shareholder meeting on December 3, 2026. There are three items up for a vote:

• Re-electing Elon Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel to the board for three-year terms.
• A non-binding say-on-pay vote on 2025 executive compensation. The compensation table lists about $158.4 billion in 2025 stock awards for Musk.
• Approving PWC as Tesla's auditor for 2026.

There is no mention of any merger with SpaceX in this proxy filing. Letter from Tesla Chair of the Board, Robyn Denholm:

"Dear Fellow Shareholders,
2026 has been a year of investment and progress for Tesla. We continued solidifying our foundation by strengthening our core vehicle, energy and services businesses as we build the infrastructure for our next phase of growth. 

We also moved closer to a future of autonomous transportation and real-world super intelligence (“SI”). This year, we began producing Cybercab at Gigafactory Texas and expanded our Robotaxi service to more U.S. cities. FSD (Supervised) usage grew exponentially as we continued to gain users and expand into new markets. We surpassed over 10 million vehicles delivered, and the Model Y remains on track to be the best-selling vehicle this year of any kind, globally, as we achieved record deliveries in countries around the world. We launched the Tesla Semi, which will revolutionize the trucking industry, and unveiled the long- awaited Next Gen Roadster. We also made progress in energy generation and storage, with record deployments out of Megafactory Shanghai and production of the new Megapack 3 at our Megafactory in Texas. As SI infrastructure demand increases, energy storage will be critical to expand capacity from the existing grid.

At the same time, we continued developing the products and investing in the infrastructure required to provide them at scale, including building our Semi factory in Nevada and the first production lines for Optimus, and additional data center capacity to train our SI systems. Our recent investments in battery and  chip manufacturing, including our Terafab initiative, will help secure the supply of critical components enabling us to offer products affordably on a mass market basis so that humanity may benefit. We remain focused on managing costs and maintaining the financial strength to support our ambitious long-term goals. 

We have accomplished a great deal, but we are still at the early stages of what we believe Tesla can become. Our employees’ innovation, hard work and dedication are essential to realizing that potential and creating lasting value for you, our shareholders. Your confidence in Tesla means a great deal to us, and we take the trust of our shareholders seriously. We listen to you, as your voices and votes help shape our governance and our future. And, as a Board, we want to continue hearing from as many of you as possible. 

That includes retail investors, who face technological barriers to traditional voting. As a result, Tesla recently pioneered the creation of user-friendly practical tools to empower the voices of retail shareholders, which provide a no-fee, investor-directed voting process similar to those currently available to institutional investors. And because we believe all retail voices should be heard across the capital markets, we have made sure the framework supporting enrollment into voluntary retail voting programs would not only be available to Tesla, but to all public companies. As we look ahead, we have the building blocks, vision and team necessary to achieve our bold yet worthwhile objectives. I am honored to serve on the Board alongside Elon Musk and JB Straubel, two technological visionaries whose leadership has helped make Tesla what it is today. The three of us are grateful to have been nominated to serve for another term on the Board of this extraordinary company. We understand that a steady and experienced hand during this time of rapid technological change is essential to Tesla’s success. Therefore, your vote is critical to maintaining that leadership, and I ask you to vote FOR our re-election to the Board so we can continue guiding Tesla through our next phase of growth. 

We have transformed numerous industries before, ranging from electric vehicles to battery storage systems. We could not be more excited to do it again, as we bring SI into the physical world. The best is yet to come.

Thank you for your continued support of Tesla. Very truly yours,
Robyn Denholm
Chair of the Board"

特斯拉正式宣布将于2026年12月3日召开年度股东大会，表决事项包括三项：

• 再次选举 Elon Musk、Robyn Denholm 和 JB Straubel 为董事会成员，任期三年。

• 批准普华永道担任特斯拉 2026 年审计师。

这份代理文件中没有提及与 SpaceX 的任何合并。特斯拉董事会主席 Robyn Denholm 致信：

“尊敬的各位股东，
2026年对于特斯拉来说是投资和进步的一年。我们通过加强核心汽车、能源和服务业务，继续巩固我们的基础，为下一阶段的增长奠定基础。 

我们还距离自动交通和现实世界超级智能（“SI”）的未来更近了。今年，我们开始在德克萨斯州 Gigafactory 生产 Cybercab，并将我们的 Robotaxi 服务扩展到更多美国城市。随着我们不断获得用户并拓展新市场，FSD（受监督）的使用量呈指数级增长。我们的交付量已超过 1000 万辆，而且 Model Y 仍有望成为今年全球最畅销的车型，因为我们在世界各国的交付量都创下了纪录。我们推出了 Tesla Semi，它将彻底改变卡车运输行业，并推出了期待已久的下一代 Roadster。我们在能源生产和存储方面也取得了进展，上海 Megafactory 的部署创纪录，并在德克萨斯州的 Megafactory 生产了新的 Megapack 3。随着SI基础设施需求的增加，储能对于扩大现有电网的容量至关重要。

与此同时，我们继续开发产品并投资大规模提供这些产品所需的基础设施，包括在内华达州建设我们的 Semi 工厂和 Optimus 的第一条生产线，以及用于培训我们的 SI 系统的额外数据中心容量。我们最近在电池和芯片制造方面的投资，包括我们的 Terafab 计划，将有助于确保关键组件的供应，使我们能够在大众市场上提供价格实惠的产品，从而使人类受益。我们仍然专注于管理成本和保持财务实力，以支持我们雄心勃勃的长期目标。 

我们已经取得了很大的成就，但我们仍处于我们相信特斯拉能够成为的早期阶段。我们员工的创新、勤奋和奉献对于实现这一潜力并为您（我们的股东）创造持久价值至关重要。您对特斯拉的信任对我们来说意义重大，我们非常重视股东的信任。我们倾听您的声音，因为您的声音和投票有助于塑造我们的治理和未来。而且，作为董事会，我们希望继续听取尽可能多的人的意见。
其中包括散户投资者，他们在传统投票方面面临技术障碍。因此，特斯拉最近率先创建了用户友好的实用工具，以赋予散户股东发声的权利，这些工具提供了类似于目前机构投资者可以使用的免费、投资者导向的投票流程。因为我们相信资本市场上应该听到所有散户的声音，所以我们确保支持自愿散户投票计划的框架不仅适用于特斯拉，也适用于所有上市公司。展望未来，我们拥有实现我们大胆而有价值的目标所需的基石、愿景和团队。我很荣幸能与埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 JB Straubel 一起在董事会任职，这两位技术梦想家的领导帮助特斯拉取得了今天的成就。我们三人很高兴被提名在这家非凡公司的董事会任职连任。我们知道，在这个技术日新月异的时代，稳定且经验丰富的人才对于特斯拉的成功至关重要。因此，您的投票对于维持这种领导地位至关重要，我请您投票支持我们连任董事会成员，以便我们能够继续引导特斯拉进入下一阶段的增长。 

我们之前已经改造了许多行业，从电动汽车到电池存储系统。当我们将 SI 带入物理世界时，我们非常高兴能再次做到这一点。最好的尚未到来。

感谢您一直以来对特斯拉的支持。非常真实的你，
罗宾·丹霍姆
